rows.title: Feeling worried and stressed
rows.description: Gauge how overwhelmed or in control you’ve felt over the last month to understand your stress levels.
rows.section1_who_content: This assessment is designed for adults 18+.
rows.section2_content:
This assessment helps you understand how stressed or overwhelmed you’ve been feeling lately, and whether life has felt manageable or out of control.

It focuses on how you’ve been responding to everyday pressures at work, at home, or personally.
rows.section3_subtitle: Understanding your mental health is the first step.

section4_notes.title: Answer based on the past month
Choose the option that fits best
There are no right or wrong answers

metadata.important_note_1: This is a self-awareness tool, not a diagnosis
metadata.important_note_2: Not intended for emergency or crisis situations
metadata.tile4_content:
What you’ll see

After completing the assessment, you’ll see:

  • A summary of how frequently stress has affected you

  • Explanation of what your stress level may indicate

  • Insight into whether stress feels situational or ongoing

  • Suggested next steps such as Equip programs, resources, or further assessments

No labels. No judgments. Just clarity.
metadata.tile5_content:
Important notes

  • This is a self-help and awareness tool, not a medical diagnosis

  • Not intended for emergency or crisis situations

  • If stress feels overwhelming or unmanageable, consider reaching out to a mental health professional

  • You may choose to share your results with a professional if helpful

rows.title: Struggling to balance life
rows.description: Pinpoint workplace stressors like workload, support, and control that may be disrupting work-life balance.
rows.section1_who_content: This assessment is designed for adults 18+.
rows.section2_content:
This assessment helps you understand how your time and energy are divided between work, rest, and the people and activities that matter to you.

It focuses on whether everyday demands have been leaving room for the rest of your life.
rows.section3_subtitle: Understanding your mental health is the first step.

metadata.tile4_content:
What you’ll see

After completing the assessment, you’ll see:

  • A summary of work-related stress and balance indicators

  • Insight into which factors (workload, control, support) feel most challenging

  • Explanation of what your results may suggest

  • Suggested next steps such as Equip programs, resources, or reflection tools

No labels. No judgments. Just clarity.
metadata.tile5_content:
Important notes

  • This is a self-help and awareness tool, not a medical or workplace diagnosis

  • Not intended for emergency or crisis situations

  • If work stress is significantly affecting your health or functioning, consider speaking with a mental health professional or trusted workplace support

  • You may choose to share your results with a professional if helpful

rows.title: Struggling with quality sleep
rows.description: An 8-question assessment to understand sleep quality, night-time patterns, and possible insomnia symptoms.
rows.section1_who_content: This assessment is designed for adults 18+.
rows.section2_content:
This assessment helps you understand your sleep patterns and how restful or disrupted your sleep has been.

It looks at both sleep quality and how sleep affects your day.
rows.section3_subtitle: Understanding your mental health is the first step.

section4_notes.title: Think about your recent sleep habits

metadata.important_note_1: Sleep issues can have many causes
metadata.important_note_2: This is a self-help assessment, not a diagnosis
metadata.tile4_content:
What you’ll see

After completing the assessment, you’ll see:

  • A summary of your sleep quality and patterns

  • Explanation of whether sleep issues appear occasional or persistent

  • Insight into how sleep may be affecting your daily life

  • Suggested next steps such as self-guided tools, Equip programs, or resources

No labels. No diagnoses. Just clarity.
metadata.tile5_content:
Important notes

  • This is a self-help and awareness tool, not a medical diagnosis

  • Not intended for emergency or crisis situations

  • If sleep problems are severe or ongoing, consider speaking with a healthcare professional

  • You may choose to share your results with a professional if helpful

rows.title: Unsure or general concern
rows.description: A quick, holistic snapshot combining anxiety, depression, well-being, resilience, and self-efficacy.
rows.section1_who_content: This assessment is designed for adults 18+.
rows.section2_content:
This assessment helps you reflect on your overall emotional state and how balanced or strained you’ve been feeling.

It focuses on emotional awareness and everyday wellbeing.
rows.section3_subtitle: Understanding your mental health is the first step.

section4_notes.title: Focus on how you’ve felt lately

metadata.tile4_content:
What you’ll see

After completing the assessment, you’ll see:

  • A simple summary of your responses

  • An overview of areas that seem stable and areas that may need attention

  • Clear explanations of what your results may indicate

  • Suggested next steps such as self-guided tools, Equip programs, or external support resources

No labels. No diagnoses. Just clarity.
metadata.tile5_content:
Important notes

  • This is a self-reflection tool, not a medical or clinical diagnosis

  • Not intended for crisis or emergency situations

  • If you’re feeling overwhelmed, distressed, or unsafe, please seek support from a mental health professional or local emergency services

  • You’re encouraged to share your results with a qualified professional if helpful

rows.title: Feeling overwhelmed and anxious
rows.description: Measure how often anxiety symptoms have affected you over the last two weeks to better understand your current stress response
rows.section1_who_content: This assessment is designed for adults 18+.
rows.section2_content:
This assessment helps you understand how frequently anxiety has been present in your life recently, including excessive worry, nervousness, and restlessness.

It focuses on how anxiety has affected your thoughts, physical sensations, and ability to manage everyday situations.
section2_bullets: Impact of worry on daily functioning
rows.section3_subtitle: Understanding your mental health is the first step.

section4_notes.title: Answer based on the past 2 weeks
Choose whAnswer based on how you’ve felt recently
Choose what best reflects your experience

metadata.important_note_2: It does not replace professional care
metadata.tile4_content:
What you’ll see

Once completed, you’ll receive:

  • A summary of how frequently anxiety symptoms have appeared

  • Clear explanation of what your score range means

  • Insight into whether anxiety seems situational or more consistent

  • Optional next steps such as self-guided tools, Equip programs, or further assessments

No labels. No judgments. Just information.
metadata.tile5_content:
How it works

  • Answer based on how you’ve felt over the past 2 weeks

  • Choose the option that fits best—there are no right or wrong answers

  • Progress is saved automatically

  • You can pause and return anytime

  • Results appear immediately after completion

rows.title: Feeling depressed and hopeless
rows.description: Reflect on how frequently depressive symptoms have impacted your mood, energy, and daily functioning recently.
rows.section1_who_content: This assessment is designed for adults 18+.
rows.section2_content:
This assessment helps you reflect on how often low mood, emotional heaviness, or loss of interest has affected you.

It focuses on emotional wellbeing and daily functioning.
rows.section3_subtitle: Understanding your mental health is the first step.

section4_notes.title: Choose what best describes your experience

metadata.important_note_1: This is not a medical diagnosis
metadata.important_note_2: If you feel distressed, seek professional support
metadata.tile4_content:
What you’ll see

After completing the assessment, you’ll see:

  • A summary of how often depressive symptoms have appeared

  • Clear explanation of what your results may suggest

  • Insight into whether symptoms seem occasional or persistent

  • Optional next steps such as Equip programs, resources, or professional support

No diagnoses. No labels. Just information to help you decide what to do next.
metadata.tile5_content:
Important notes

  • This is a self-help and awareness tool, not a medical diagnosis

  • Not intended for emergency or crisis situations

  • If you’re feeling unsafe, hopeless, or at risk of harming yourself, seek immediate help from local emergency services or a mental health professional

  • You’re encouraged to discuss your results with a qualified professional if helpful

rows.title: Feeling drained and burned out
rows.description: Identify emotional exhaustion and mental distance related to work stress as a first step toward recovery.
rows.section1_who_content: This assessment is designed for adults 18+.
rows.section2_content:
This assessment helps you identify signs of burnout, including exhaustion, detachment, and reduced motivation.

It focuses on how prolonged stress may be affecting your work and personal life.
rows.section3_subtitle: Understanding your mental health is the first step.

section4_notes.title: Reflect on sustained patterns, not one bad day
Answer based on your typical experience

metadata.important_note_1: Burnout can build gradually over time
metadata.important_note_2: This assessment is for awareness, not diagnosis
metadata.tile4_content:
What you’ll see

After completing the assessment, you’ll see:

  • A summary of burnout-related signals

  • Insight into which dimensions (energy, motivation, mental distance) feel most affected

  • Explanation of what your results may suggest

  • Optional next steps such as Equip programs, resources, or professional support

No labels. No judgments. Just perspective.
metadata.tile5_content:
Important notes

  • This is a self-help and awareness tool, not a medical diagnosis

  • Not intended for emergency or crisis situations

  • If burnout feels severe, persistent, or is affecting your ability to function, consider speaking with a mental health professional

  • You may choose to share your results with a professional if helpful
